title: Three-Way Merge Without Duplicates

description.intro: Given three sorted arrays, arr1, arr2, and arr3, return a new array with the elements of all three arrays, in sorted order, without duplicates.
examples:
Example 1:
Input:
arr1 = [2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 7]
arr2 = [3, 3, 9]
arr3 = [3, 3, 9]
Output: [2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9]
Explanation: The value 3 appears multiple times in the input but only once in
the output.

Example 2:
Input:
arr1 = [1, 2, 3]
arr2 = [2, 3, 4]
arr3 = [3, 4, 5]
Output: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Explanation: Each duplicate value is included only once.

Example 3:
Input:
arr1 = [1, 1, 1, 1]
arr2 = [1, 1, 1]
arr3 = [1, 1]
Output: [1]
Explanation: All ones are merged into a single occurrence.
constraints: The input arrays are sorted in ascending order
description.approach:
This is a three-pointer problem that extends the 'two-array merge' idea to handle three arrays and remove duplicates. We can track the current position in each array and always take the smallest value among them, while being careful to skip duplicates.

The algorithm uses three pointers:

p1: current position in arr1
p2: current position in arr2
p3: current position in arr3
At each step:

Find the minimum value among the current elements of all arrays
Advance the pointer(s) pointing to this value
Add the minimum value to the result if it's different from the last added value
Continue until all arrays are exhausted
This problem is good practice for index manipulation:

We need to handle cases where arrays have different lengths
We need to skip duplicates both within and across arrays
We need to handle empty arrays and arrays with all the same values

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n1: the length of arr1

n2: the length of arr2

n3: the length of arr3

Time: O(n1 + n2 + n3) - at each iteration, at least one pointer advances, so the total number of iterations is at most the sum of all array lengths

Extra space: O(n1 + n2 + n3) - for the output array
